races.name: RF Miller & Co Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
Hadwins Mares' Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Fair Damsel
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner here and likely to get an uncontested lead; eight-year-old mares' performer with solid Good-ground form and blinkers on, but the [STYLE_FIT] flag means she is technically racing out of her sharpest role — her chance depends entirely on how well she can dominate and conserve at Cartmel's tight track over 2m6f.

runners_data.name: Victoria Milano
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up operator with a strong recent record including two places on Good ground over similar trips, handled well by Toby Wynne; the Cartmel circuit's tight bends may catch her out if she needs a long run to find her stride, but her trainer Greenall/Guerriero yard is 5/21 in the last 14 days.

runners_data.name: Belles Benefit
runners_data.note: Prominent racer whose Good-ground form over this sort of trip reads well (2W4P at similar conditions), though 236 days off the track is a significant concern; blinkers noted, Ben Case yard quiet in the 14-day window, and she will need a first-time-back performance to win.

runners_data.name: Blackwater Lilly
runners_data.note: True hold-up type with consistent Good-ground form at similar distances for Neil King, posting a series of solid placed efforts; Jack Quinlan takes the ride and she is the freshest of the genuine closers here, but Cartmel's configuration limits how much ground can realistically be made up.

runners_data.name: Gerrys Wish
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott-trained five-year-old racing prominently who has finished placed in her last three Good-ground starts, and Sean Bowen's booking is a notable upgrade; the step up to 2m6f is untested but her staying profile suits, and she is perhaps the most interesting hold on the prominent racer.

runners_data.name: Turkey And Ham
runners_data.note: Prominent type with a win on Good ground at 18f earlier in this form string; Mr D McGill claims 5lbs, which softens the weight, but 67 days off the track and the trainer's quiet 14-day stats (0/4) make her form hard to fully rely on here.

runners_data.name: Parish Star
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who has won twice recently but both wins came on Soft or Heavier ground; her sim-going record on Good is just 2/15 and Joshua Thompson claims 5lbs, so the Going is a potential question mark even if the distance is familiar.

runners_data.name: Forest Spirit
runners_data.note: Five-year-old whose natural style is to race prominently — held up here in the map because there are too many hold-up types for the rear positions to absorb; the REDISTRIBUTED and STYLE_FIT flags mean his mapped position flatters his actual tactical situation, and James Bowen will likely settle him further back than suits him best.

runners_data.name: Alvesta
runners_data.note: Won most recently at 17f on Good ground and Brian Hughes takes a strong ride; classed as a hold-up type but mapped to midfield due to field congestion at the rear — she races wide of her comfort zone positionally, though her low OR of 80 and recent winning form give her an each-way profile if she gets a clean passage.

runners_data.name: Masonbrook Meadow
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with Good-ground placed form at 22-24f who is another genuine hold-up runner pushed up the positional map by the density of closers in this field; Benjamin Macey claims 5lbs, the trainer Seamus Mullins is 3/11 in the 14-day window, but the REDISTRIBUTED tag means she is unlikely to secure the position the map shows her in.

races.paceDynamic: Fair Damsel is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner mares' handicap hurdle over 2m6f on Good ground at Cartmel, and with no genuine rival prepared to press her from the front, she is likely to control proceedings at a fair but sustainable gallop throughout. Gerrys Wish, Belles Benefit, and Turkey And Ham will track her in the prominent positions, creating a compact early order that shapes into a steadily-run contest rather than a searching test of stamina. The true hold-up brigade — Forest Spirit, Alvesta, and Masonbrook Meadow — have been pushed up the map because this field is heavier with hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate; in reality all three are likely to race further back than their mapped position suggests, making late ground-eating runs harder to execute on Cartmel's tight turning track. This race shape strongly favours horses racing prominently or tracking the leader into the straight, where the lack of a genuine pace injector means those travelling smoothly in the slipstream of Fair Damsel will be best positioned when the tempo lifts at the final two hurdles.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Fair Damsel Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Fair Damsel bowls along unchallenged and the prominent trackers lack the acceleration to reel her in.
scenarios.body: If Fair Damsel bowls along unchallenged and the prominent trackers lack the acceleration to reel her in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Fair Damsel's advantage is pegged back in the final half-mile and a prominent stalker pounces at the last.
scenarios.body: If Fair Damsel's advantage is pegged back in the final half-mile and a prominent stalker pounces at the last.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sharply enough from the second-last to string the field out and create a gap for a late finisher.
scenarios.body: If the pace quickens sharply enough from the second-last to string the field out and create a gap for a late finisher.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Outsider Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If Fair Damsel sets a frantic pace and weakens sharply, leaving the door open for a mid-pack horse to coast through.
scenarios.body: If Fair Damsel sets a frantic pace and weakens sharply, leaving the door open for a mid-pack horse to coast through.

watchPoints.text: Fair Damsel's lead — if she gets even five lengths clear by halfway, no rival on this track configuration is likely to run her down before the last, making her positional dominance the single biggest race-shaping factor.

Forest Spirit, Alvesta, and Masonbrook Meadow are all genuine hold-up horses pushed into mapped midfield positions; if all three drift back to their natural position, the rear of the field could become congested and all three may face traffic issues on the final bend.

Belles Benefit returns from 236 days off and her chance depends on whether she bounces straight back to form — watch her in the paddock and early in the race to see if she travels with her usual fluency.
Gerrys Wish's booking of Sean Bowen from the Gordon Elliott yard (8/45 in 14 days) represents the most significant jockey-trainer combination uplift in the field and merits monitoring in the market.

Cartmel's tight, undulating circuit over 2m6f typically amplifies the advantage of prominent racers who jump well — any horse seen making errors at hurdles early will likely lose too much ground to recover on this track.

races.name: Molson Coors Novices' Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Settle Down Jill
runners_data.note: A prominent-travelling mare with an OR of 111 and an excellent record on Good ground (2 wins, 8 places from 15 runs), trained by Tristan Davidson who has 2 from 8 over 14 days — she finished 1st and 3rd in her last two Good-ground runs and at only 19 days since last run should be race-fit; the key question is whether she has the pace to match Passengerontheship off the front.

runners_data.name: Passengerontheship
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner with four consecutive wins including three over Good ground, trained by Sam England (4/15 T14), wearing a tongue-tie, and only 5 days since his last run — his ability to dictate an uncontested lead is the dominant factor in how this race is run from flag to finish.

runners_data.name: Back In The Bay
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator with three wins over Good ground and Jonathan Burke in the saddle, last seen finishing 7th at Huntingdon 34 days ago — his best form suggests he stays well and can finish strongly, but he needs Passengerontheship to tire considerably before the last to have a realistic winning chance.

runners_data.name: Justicialism
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old hold-up type wearing a tongue-piece, trained by Noel Kelly who is 0 from 4 over 14 days, and tagged with a finishing fade warning — he has hit the frame four times on Good ground without winning, suggesting a limiting ceiling rather than a potential winner against a leader on a going day.

runners_data.name: Aslukgoes
runners_data.note: A prominent racer with headgear (p) who has shown better form on Good than Soft and is partnered by Sean Bowen — 37 days between runs is not ideal, and recent form of 4th, 6th, 7th suggests he is finding it hard to win off his current mark, but he could contest second if Passengerontheship is caught.

runners_data.name: Jack Sprat
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse by profile whose natural position at the rear is compromised in this race shape — his OR of 98 and recent form of 9th, 4th, 7th reflect the difficulty of making ground from off a steady pace, and racing in a midfield slot rather than his preferred position reduces his already modest winning prospects.

races.paceDynamic: Passengerontheship is the sole confirmed front-runner and, on current form, has won four of his last five over Good ground — he will stride to the front from the off and set a measured, controlling tempo over the 2m5f trip at Cartmel. With no genuine rival willing to challenge for the lead, he is likely to dictate on his own terms, conserving energy through the first circuit before quickening away from the final bend. Settle Down Jill and Aslukgoes will be keen to push forward into prominent positions, meaning the early stages will not be entirely devoid of pressure, but neither is a true pace horse and both are likely to settle behind Passengerontheship rather than contest the front. This race shape — a lone, unchallenged leader setting a sustainable gallop — strongly favours the front-runner himself and any prominent racer with the stamina to sit just off the pace and strike at the second-last, rather than hold-up horses who will need the pace to collapse to come from off the bridle. The field holds more hold-up types than can realistically get a clear run from the rear; Jack Sprat is a genuine hold-up horse redistributed to midfield on the map, and is unlikely to secure the position that suits him best, making a late-swooping finish from that quarter a lower-probability outcome.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Passengerontheship leads unchallenged and sets a rhythm that never truly tests his stamina reserves.
scenarios.body: If Passengerontheship leads unchallenged and sets a rhythm that never truly tests his stamina reserves.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Settle Down Jill or Aslukgoes press Passengerontheship more than expected and he weakens approaching the last.
scenarios.body: If Settle Down Jill or Aslukgoes press Passengerontheship more than expected and he weakens approaching the last.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closer Stalks And Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely strong enough to set up a late finish and a hold-up horse finds a clear passage.
scenarios.body: If the pace proves genuinely strong enough to set up a late finish and a hold-up horse finds a clear passage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Attrition Chaos From Rear
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or fallers disrupt the front group and a hold-up type inherits a position late on.
scenarios.body: If jumping errors or fallers disrupt the front group and a hold-up type inherits a position late on.

watchPoints.text: Passengerontheship jumps from stall at price — if he misses a fence early and surrenders the lead, the entire race shape collapses and Settle Down Jill or Back In The Bay become immediate dangers.

Settle Down Jill at OR 111 is the highest-rated runner and her trainer Davidson has two winners from eight over 14 days — if she travels into the race more sweetly than Passengerontheship she could lead him into the straight and overhaul him on the run-in.

Back In The Bay's jockey Jonathan Burke is a high-class navigator around tight tracks like Cartmel — watch for him hunting the rail on the final turn to manufacture a run that his hold-up style would otherwise struggle to find in a small field.

Justicialism's "fades in finish" flag is significant at Cartmel where the uphill run to the line exposes stamina limitations — he may look dangerous at the last but punters should be cautious if backing him to hold on.

Jack Sprat's headgear (p) and redistribution to midfield means he is unlikely to be seen in contention at any stage — his form figures of 9-4-7 at similar trips on Good ground suggest he is one to note as a market drifter rather than a beneficiary of this pace shape.

races.name: Lakes Luxury Loo's Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Caughtinyourtrance
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter ridden by Brian Hughes for James Moffatt; Good-ground form reads 2W from 5 similar runs but the STYLE_FIT flag tempers confidence — if prominent trackers close her down efficiently, she is vulnerable in the final stages despite the tactical advantage of leading.

runners_data.name: Red Happy
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old with a striking three-win record over 2m4f on Good ground, making this step up to 3m1½f the key unknown; the refusal and rider-off entries on the form line are a slight worry, but if fit and jumping cleanly under Jonathon Bewley this trip on Good ground looks within reach.

runners_data.name: Stratagem
runners_data.note: Dual Cartmel winner over 3m on Good ground with Mickey Bowen's yard in strong form (5/30 in 14 days) and tongue-tie applied; amateur rider Mr James Murray claims 7lb which is significant, but the horse's track record here and proven stamina make him a central figure in the prominent-tracking scenario.

runners_data.name: Tiger Orchid
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse — the only true H-style runner in this field — with the best sim-going strike rate of any runner here (12/15 on Good or similar); blinkers applied and fresh off a 22-day break, but needs a genuinely strong pace to close into, and that is not guaranteed with a lone, unhurried leader.

runners_data.name: Ivane
runners_data.note: Strong traveller who naturally wants to race prominently but is mapped back into midfield by the crowd of prominent types; visor fitted and Jonathan Burke takes the ride for James Owen's busy yard (6/51), but a recent record of five consecutive fourths over longer trips on yielding ground raises a question about his ability to get competitive from a compromised position here.

runners_data.name: Fairlawn Flyer
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old running alongside stablemate Stratagem for Mickey Bowen and Sean Bowen — a significant jockey booking — and has placed form at 3m on Good ground, but is a natural front-runner who will find himself racing out of role in this shape; the pulled-up run on soft ground over 4m last time needs ignoring if conditions are the explanation.

runners_data.name: Le Grand Vert
runners_data.note: Won his most recent start over 25f on Good ground for Noel C Kelly (fresh, just 20 days ago) and has shown he can win fresh, but is another genuine prominent type who will be pushed further back than he wants; the 5lb claimer Mr O McGill and a low trainer 14-day strike rate (0/3) add risk to what is already a compromised tactical position.

races.paceDynamic: Caughtinyourtrance is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival likely to press for the lead, should settle into a comfortable, uncontested gallop over this 3m1½f trip on Good ground at Cartmel — a track where a controlled pace from the front is notoriously hard to peg back. Red Happy, Stratagem, and Caughtinyourtrance herself will occupy the prominent positions just behind, while the field contains more front-running and prominent types than can realistically secure their natural berth: Ivane, Fairlawn Flyer, and Le Grand Vert are all genuine prominent racers who are likely to find themselves shuffled back into a midfield role they do not naturally suit. The resulting shape — a single relaxed pace-setter, a cluster of prominent types just off the leader, and a tail of horses racing out of role — strongly favours runners who can track the pace comfortably from the second or third position and sustain their effort over the final circuit, rather than those who rely on a truly searching gallop to bring hold-up horses into play.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front-runner controls, tracks win
scenarios.trigger: If Caughtinyourtrance sets an unchallenged, economical gallop and the prominent trackers travel smoothly throughout.
scenarios.body: If Caughtinyourtrance sets an unchallenged, economical gallop and the prominent trackers travel smoothly throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace injected, stamina test
scenarios.trigger: If one or more of the redistributed prominent types — Ivane, Fairlawn Flyer, or Le Grand Vert — fights for position early and injects genuine pace into the race.
scenarios.body: If one or more of the redistributed prominent types — Ivane, Fairlawn Flyer, or Le Grand Vert — fights for position early and injects genuine pace into the race.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Redistribution chaos, closers pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the three displaced prominent types — Ivane, Fairlawn Flyer, Le Grand Vert — collectively create a messy, stop-start early gallop that burns out the principals.
scenarios.body: If the three displaced prominent types — Ivane, Fairlawn Flyer, Le Grand Vert — collectively create a messy, stop-start early gallop that burns out the principals.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Lone leader quickens clear
scenarios.trigger: If Caughtinyourtrance is allowed to steal a decisive advantage turning for home and none of the prominent trackers have the tactical speed to respond.
scenarios.body: If Caughtinyourtrance is allowed to steal a decisive advantage turning for home and none of the prominent trackers have the tactical speed to respond.

watchPoints.text: Stratagem's dual course-and-distance winning form at Cartmel combined with Bowen's yard in hot form makes him the most dangerous prominent tracker if Caughtinyourtrance sets a comfortable pace — watch whether Mr James Murray settles him efficiently in the first mile.

Red Happy's form figures show three wins from six at 24f on Good ground but his last two runs ended in a refusal and a rider-off — if he jumps cleanly from the off under Jonathon Bewley, that underlying form makes him a major threat; any early jumping hesitation is a critical tell.

Monitor how Ivane, Fairlawn Flyer, and Le Grand Vert — all natural front-runners — jump off at the start; if two or more immediately contest for the early gallop, the pace dynamic shifts sharply from scenario A toward scenario B and Tiger Orchid becomes significantly more relevant.

Tiger Orchid's effectiveness is almost entirely dependent on the tempo being strong enough for a hold-up horse to close into — if Caughtinyourtrance is allowed to bowl along at her own rhythm, watch whether Charlie Hammond attempts to move earlier than ideal rather than getting left too far behind.

Le Grand Vert won 20 days ago and returns quickly under a 5lb claimer for a trainer with just 0/3 in the 14-day window — a sharp watch on his pre-race behaviour and early jumping would confirm whether the quick turnaround has left him fresh and dangerous or flat.

races.name: Holker Homes Handicap Chase

runners_data.name: Thank You Blue
runners_data.note: Confirmed front runner for Jennie Candlish, 17 days since a win over a shorter trip; Good ground is fine and Cartmel suits a bold jumper who leads, but the style-fit tag at 0.93 means he is technically racing out of role in the pace map — treat his chance on merit as the race's primary pace setter, which is exactly his natural profile.

runners_data.name: Blue Reed
runners_data.note: Recent winner at Cartmel (19f, Good) for Irish handler Cian Collins is the standout form angle; prominent racer who should track the leader comfortably in the front group, and that course-and-going combination gives him a legitimate live chance if he reproduces that effort.

runners_data.name: Zumbi
runners_data.note: James Moffatt runner with strong recent form — two wins and a second in last three starts including Good-ground victories; the apprentice claim from Leah Noreci (10lb) is a factor, and as a confirmed prominent racer with the best current form in the race he is a serious threat from a front-rank position.

runners_data.name: Am Still Here
runners_data.note: Nicky Richards five-year-old returning from a 266-day absence, which is the single biggest flag against him; consistent placed form including a second at 2m4f on Good, but Sean Quinlan takes the ride and the lengthy layoff from a prominent-style chaser is a sizeable risk at this trip.

runners_data.name: Tell Me Again
runners_data.note: Micky Hammond hold-up horse whose last five runs on Good ground produced two unknowns, an eighth, a fourth and a tenth — the sim-going record on this surface is modest; Conor O'Farrell rides and without a strong gallop to close into, this type of race shape is likely to leave him with too much ground to make up.

runners_data.name: Judicial Review
runners_data.note: Brian Hughes partners this Moffatt horse, a natural prominent racer whose redistribution into midfield on the map reflects field congestion rather than his instincts — he will look to race closer than shown, and his two Good-ground runs this season (sixth and a win over 21f) suggest the conditions are fine; the style-fit discount is the operative caution.

runners_data.name: Out On Her Own
runners_data.note: Dianne Sayer hold-up mare who has placed five times in last six starts without winning; Ryan Mania rides and the consistent placed profile is appealing, but she needs the pace to be genuine enough to deliver a meaningful late run, and a one-dimensional front runner at the head of affairs makes that uncertain.

runners_data.name: Roi Du Roume
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen takes the mount for his father Mickey, and the trainer has six runners in the past 14 days from 34 runs — a busy, form-forward yard; hold-up profile needs cut in the pace but three Good-ground runs this season all produced placings, and the booking of Sean Bowen lifts interest.

runners_data.name: Mr Globalist
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse for Lizzie Quinlan mapped to midfield because of rear-group congestion — the redistribution note is secondary to the fact that his last nine starts on Good ground produced zero wins and only two placings; Peter Kavanagh rides and the form string of consecutive fourths and fifths is consistent but uninspiring.

runners_data.name: On The Platform
runners_data.note: Non-runner: listed as such in the data, so any tactical assessment is moot; natural prominent type for Belinda Clarke who would have competed for a front-rank position but does not take part.

races.paceDynamic: Thank You Blue is the one confirmed front runner here and on Good ground at Cartmel over 2m5f, a horse who leads from the front and is uncontested sets a sustainable, measured tempo that is unlikely to be truly searching. Blue Reed, Zumbi, and Am Still Here are all natural prominent racers who will push to sit just off the pace, creating a compact lead group but not a war for position — the gallop should be honest rather than frenetic. The field contains more pace-minded types than the map can accommodate: Judicial Review and On The Platform are genuine prominent horses shuffled into a midfield mapping by congestion, while Mr Globalist is a true hold-up type also displaced in the diagram — those three are unlikely to run from their mapped positions, meaning the actual prominent slots will be hard-fought in the early stages. A controlled, front-running tempo on Good ground at a tight track like Cartmel strongly favours prominent racers with tactical fluency and jumping accuracy, particularly those proven on this going and who can travel comfortably into contention through the final circuit.

scenarios.title: Front Runner Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Thank You Blue leads uncontested and the prominent group settles without serious pressure, dictating a fair but manageable pace.
scenarios.body: If Thank You Blue leads uncontested and the prominent group settles without serious pressure, dictating a fair but manageable pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pack Wears Down Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Blue Reed or Zumbi push hard enough in the back straight to take the race to Thank You Blue and expose a weakness in the final climb.
scenarios.body: If Blue Reed or Zumbi push hard enough in the back straight to take the race to Thank You Blue and expose a weakness in the final climb.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely strong enough to burn off the leaders and leave a clear passage for a closer to rattle home.
scenarios.body: If the early pace is genuinely strong enough to burn off the leaders and leave a clear passage for a closer to rattle home.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Drifter Finds Gap
scenarios.trigger: If the race is messy up front, with scrimmaging among the prominent pack creating traffic and a horse picking through late from an unexpected position.
scenarios.body: If the race is messy up front, with scrimmaging among the prominent pack creating traffic and a horse picking through late from an unexpected position.

watchPoints.text: Thank You Blue's uncontested lead is the fulcrum of the entire race — if he jumps cleanly and bowls along at a comfortable clip, he could be very hard to pass on Cartmel's tight finish, and any prominent rival who tries to go with him too early risks burning out.

Zumbi and Blue Reed both want to race prominently and will compete for the same ground behind the leader in the early stages — watch for a scrimmage between them from the start that could unsettle one or both before the halfway point.

Am Still Here returns from 266 days off; Sean Quinlan is an accomplished jump jockey but a prominent-style chaser resuming after nine months at a handicap mark can be unpredictable in the first half and may take a keen hold or jump out of rhythm, creating interference risk for those around him.

Roi Du Roume with Sean Bowen in the saddle for the Bowen family operation is worth monitoring from a market movement perspective — the jockey booking is a significant upgrade and if the market reacts before the off it signals stable confidence in a horse who otherwise looks held on a hold-up profile.

races.name: Cartmel Priory Cofe School Amateur Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Garrick Painter
runners_data.note: Held-up runner with a win over 16f on Good ground in last relevant similar outing, but a 41-day break, a Cartmel fade-in-finish flag, and a high weight of 168lbs are collective concerns for a pure closer in a moderate-pace race.

runners_data.name: Envious Editor
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old with four consecutive placed efforts but a 420-day absence (including a point-to-point break) is a significant red flag; naturally wants to race off a strong pace from the rear but this field's shape means that target may not materialise, blunting its closing opportunity despite solid Going-form figures.

runners_data.name: Lightening Company
runners_data.note: Has won on Good at 12f and 10f in past — shorter-trip specialist — making this 2m1f trip at Cartmel a likely stamina query; 307 days off the track adds considerable fitness doubt regardless of style.

runners_data.name: Jolie Coeur Allen
runners_data.note: Genuinely consistent performer at 17f on Good ground with a win and multiple places in similar conditions; races from the rear but has the tactical adaptability and relevant course-distance profile to make a bold show if the pace scenario suits, and Ben Haslam's stable is in form (1/14 last 14 days).

runners_data.name: Dog Fox
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner who shaped as the pace-setter on Good ground 13 of its last 15 runs; a Cartmel track-specialist profile suits making all, though the STYLE_FIT tag notes it may need things to go right and the 41-day break is worth monitoring.

runners_data.name: Goodwin Face
runners_data.note: Chris Gordon-trained six-year-old with an admirable recent form string (1-2-2-3) — all on Good ground — who races prominently and can press Dog Fox without overcommitting; Henry Main's 5lb claim is a meaningful weight advantage in a competitive amateur race.

runners_data.name: Book Of Secrets
runners_data.note: Consistent but modest performer whose last seven results show no better than fourth; true hold-up horse whose style is compromised here by the moderate pace Dog Fox will set, and sim-going figures of 0W3P in similar conditions cap expectations.

runners_data.name: Dusky Days
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old who has shown best form at 22-26f trips — this 2m1f trip is conspicuously shorter than its recent campaign distances; its natural closing style is further undermined by a moderate-pace scenario, making a forward showing unlikely despite two wins on similar ground.

runners_data.name: Zamond
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old who has raced prominently on Good in the past and has two recent wins (both on Good) to call upon; Donald McCain's stable is active (2/26 last 14 days) and Zamond pressing Dog Fox for the lead is the most realistic challenge to front-running supremacy.

runners_data.name: Out Out
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton inmate returning after a massive 441-day absence (including 404 days point-to-pointing); last win came on Soft ground at 16f and the fitness question mark after such a long break is severe regardless of its natural style.

runners_data.name: Blue Siam
runners_data.note: Listed as non-runner — disregard for race shape analysis; four-year-old with consistent form figures of 3-4-4-5-5 all on Good ground suggests it stays in the mix when it does run.

races.paceDynamic: Dog Fox is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival for the lead in this 11-runner amateur handicap hurdle, should dictate from the outset at a controlled, self-set tempo on Good ground at Cartmel. Goodwin Face and Zamond are the most likely prominent challengers, sitting close enough to apply some pressure, but neither has the profile to force a true war for the lead. The pace should therefore be honest-to-moderate rather than punishing, making it difficult for horses off the pace to generate a meaningful late run on a tight, undulating circuit that already blunts finishing kicks. This shape strongly favours hold-up types who can track closer than usual and horses who can race prominently without burning their engine — pure deep closers are disadvantaged because the redistribution note flags that most of the perceived hold-up horses in this field (Envious Editor, Book Of Secrets, Dusky Days, Out Out, Blue Siam) are genuine late-runners who will struggle to get a true target to peg back at a moderate tempo; the horses most likely to secure a forward position ahead of them are Dog Fox, Goodwin Face, and Zamond, giving a front-running/prominent profile the clearest tactical edge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dog Fox Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Dog Fox bowls along uncontested and sets a measured pace that denies the closers a target to run at.
scenarios.body: If Dog Fox bowls along uncontested and sets a measured pace that denies the closers a target to run at.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fight It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Goodwin Face or Zamond press Dog Fox hard enough to force an attritional early tempo.
scenarios.body: If Goodwin Face or Zamond press Dog Fox hard enough to force an attritional early tempo.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Late
scenarios.trigger: If Dog Fox sets a genuinely fast gallop that prematurely burns itself out and leaves a meaningful gap for closers.

watchPoints.text: Dog Fox — if Miss Antonia Heraghty elects to ease the pace aggressively through the back straight, the race could collapse into a sprint finish that Dog Fox wins without being truly tested, removing the chance of any true hold-up horse landing a blow.

Goodwin Face — watch whether Henry Main pushes forward to press Dog Fox or settles mid-prominently; how aggressively he attacks the pace in the first mile will define whether Scenario A or Scenario B unfolds.

Jolie Coeur Allen — if held up too far off the pace by Mr John Dawson on a tight, turning Cartmel circuit, it risks being unable to find daylight in the straight; its scenario-relevance depends heavily on a forward enough position from the outset.

Envious Editor — with 420 days off the track and a true hold-up profile in a race that lacks a strong pace to chase, watch the market move late as an indicator of whether connections have it race-fit enough to warrant serious consideration.

Out Out — monitor any significant market move for this Dan Skelton runner returning from 441 days off; if well-backed despite the absence, Skelton's team may have it significantly more forward in its preparation than the layoff suggests.
